Which variables carry the regime structure?

Cluster structure of the 14 CE scenarios, block by block — LEEDS_MODEL

Published

September 10, 2026

The short version

Six variable blocks, 14 scenarios, long-term (t + 20) deviations in the joint (Z1, Z2) space. Every block carries structure better than a column-shuffled null. But they do not carry the same amount of it, and the difference falls exactly along the macro / non-macro line.

1 · How many groups does each block support?

Real activity peaks at k = 5, Fiscal at k = 4, Finance & wealth at k = 3. Every non-macro block peaks at k = 2. The published five-regime taxonomy is visible in the data — but only through the macro-financial variables.

2 · Do different blocks find the same groups?

Real activity, Fiscal, Finance & wealth, External and Labour & distribution all return {1,3,4,6,7,8,9,11,12} against {2,5,10,13,14} — at ARI 1.00, from five disjoint sets of variables. Ecological returns something else entirely (ARI 0.11): it splits {everything} from {Sc5}.

3 · The trees

4 · The scenario map, and why Sc5 is not a regime member

Sc5’s nearest neighbour is Sc14 at 11.22 — farther than the mean pairwise distance of 8.58. It has no close neighbour at all. From Sc14’s side, Sc5 ranks 12th of 13: Sc14’s actual neighbours are Sc2 (6.22) and Sc10 (6.90). For contrast, Symmetric Contraction is an order of magnitude tighter: d(Sc6,Sc12) = 0.63, d(Sc8,Sc12) = 0.66.

So Construction Rebound groups two scenarios that share a mechanism — the investment multiplier — but not an outcome profile. Sc5 is an isolate; Sc14 belongs with the fossil and metals scenarios.

5 · Drop the two construction scenarios and three clusters fall out

On the 12, k = 3 returns {1,4,9} · {2,10,13} · {3,6,7,8,11,12} — Production Leakage, the divergence group, Symmetric Contraction — with no singletons. On all 14, k = 3 instead returns {sym nine} · {2,10,13,14} · {5}: one of the three “clusters” is Sc5 alone.

The five-regime taxonomy is three regimes plus two outliers.

6 · ANOVA: which variables actually discriminate the regimes?

Read the right panel against the left. Under the three-regime taxonomy the discriminating variables are consumption (η² 0.965), final demand (0.964), debt/GDP (0.960), taxes (0.959) and public debt (0.957) — real activity and the fiscal block, all above 0.95.

And the ecological variables collapse. Emissions falls 0.853 → 0.336, cumulative CO₂ 0.778 → 0.379, materials 0.642 → 0.077 — none significant once Sc5 and Sc14 are out. Land (0.157) and water (0.228) never discriminated under either taxonomy.

The current account is not in this figure, and that is a correction. An earlier version of this report scored cab at η² = 0.137 and read it as a weak signal. It is not a weak signal: it is structurally absent. Z1_cab = -Z2_cab holds exactly, so the two regions’ percentage deviations are identical scenario by scenario and the divergence is zero — measured sd 1.9e-14 against sd 1.05 for the Z1 deviation itself. The number being scored was floating-point residue. tb and g cancel the same way (sd exactly 0) and were already excluded by the zero-variance guard; cab slipped through because its residue has variance ~4e-28, which is greater than zero. The guard is now a tolerance. qmd/cross_border_analysis.qmd had this right already and drops all three from divergence space.

So the ecological block’s apparent regime signal was the two construction scenarios. Removing them leaves the ecological variables with no regime structure at all — which is the same result Figure 2 gives by a different route (ARI 0.11), and it is the sharpest thing in this report.

7 · Does any of this survive the tariff-base correction?

Everything above is computed on the submitted arm — the specification as published, in which equation 5.4 assesses tariff revenue on a real import volume times the tariff rate and books it as nominal revenue, omitting the foreign price vector and the (1 + tar) divisor. Two corrected arms exist: author_variant (foreign market price, with the divisor) and customs (foreign pre-VAT price with the divisor — the destination principle, and the classically correct base).

Re-running sections 5 and 6 on all three arms:

submitted author_variant customs
best k, 12 scenarios 2 (0.576) 2 (0.577) 2 (0.578)
the k = 3 partition {1,4,9} {2,10,13} {3,6,7,8,11,12} identical identical
ARI against submitted — 1.0000 1.0000

The three-regime result is invariant to the correction. So is the ANOVA, for 34 of 35 variables: mean |Δη²| between submitted and customs is 0.011, and every ecological conclusion in section 6 moves by less than 0.004.

The apparent exception was cab, whose η² read 0.019 / 0.137 / 0.435 across the three arms — a range of 0.42. That is not tariff sensitivity. cab’s divergence is structurally zero (sd 1.9e-14), so all three numbers are η² computed on floating-point residue, and residue is not arm-invariant because it is not a quantity. With cab correctly excluded, the ANOVA is invariant to the tariff correction across every variable it can legitimately score: the largest remaining movement is gdef at |Δη²| = 0.041, which does not change its significance or its ranking.

Worth recording, because it refutes a plausible-sounding explanation: the two regions’ cab baselines rescale by identical factors (×1.1620 under author_variant, ×1.3580 under customs, Z1 and Z2 alike), so the differential-rescaling story does not apply here. gdef is the variable where the regional factors genuinely differ (×1.5978 vs ×1.6178, and ×2.3730 vs ×2.4198).

What this says for the revision — revised

  1. Report three regimes plus two named outliers, not five. {1,4,9} Production Leakage, {2,10,13} asymmetric divergence, {3,6,7,8,11,12} Symmetric Contraction — clean, no singletons, and the pooled silhouette improves from 0.504 to 0.576 when Sc5 and Sc14 come out.
  2. The two-mode reduction remains the most robust result — five disjoint blocks recover it at ARI 1.00.
  3. The regimes are macro-financial objects. The 3–5 fine structure lives in output, deficits and balance sheets; the discriminating variables are consumption, final demand, debt and taxes.
  4. The ecological variables do not track the regimes, and what looked like ecological discrimination was Sc5 and Sc14. For a paper arguing an ecological–macroeconomic trilemma this needs saying directly rather than being left implicit.
  5. Never report an η² for cab, tb or g in divergence space. All three cancel bilaterally and have no divergence to explain. This is an exclusion by accounting identity, not a weak result — and stating it as “the current account does not discriminate the regimes” would be wrong in a way a referee would catch.
  6. Sc5 and Sc14 deserve their own treatment — as an investment-channel case study, not as a fifth regime.
